Transgender drama prevails once again, but it begs the question- body dysmorphia or transgenderism?

Becoming transgender can be a way of solving extreme body dysmorphia. Not everyone with body dysmorphia, however, will become transgender to solve their problem. It manifests in more than one way. And to be fair to everyone's opinion, I think the whole argument of "you can't get a sex change!" "Yes that can happen!" are being argued from two totally different points. On one hand, you cannot change your DNA to be XY if you have XX, which most of the "it's impossible to get a sex change" arguments are coming from, and on the other hand, it's possible to have procedures done to fit in more socially (look more alike, have a body similarly shaped, voice changes, that kind of thing) and be accepted by (going with our XX to XY example) other men socially- in essence, becoming a man. So for what each argument is, they're both right. It's not possible to change your chromosomes, but it is possible to be accepted socially into a group, even if that's a group as broad as "men" is.
